response.sql:
WITH matched_data AS (
  SELECT 
    tr.transreg,
    tr.ordertypedist,
    sf.shortintrt,
    sf.optvolrt
  FROM transactionrecord tr
  INNER JOIN sentimentandfundamentals sf ON sf.transref = tr.transreg
),
transaction_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    transreg,
    ordertypedist,
    AVG(shortintrt) as avg_shortintrt,
    AVG(optvolrt) as avg_optvolrt
  FROM matched_data
  GROUP BY transreg, ordertypedist
),
baseline_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    ordertypedist,
    AVG(shortintrt) as baseline_shortintrt
  FROM matched_data
  GROUP BY ordertypedist
)
SELECT 
  ta.transreg,
  ta.ordertypedist,
  ta.avg_shortintrt,
  ta.avg_optvolrt,
  CASE 
    WHEN ba.baseline_shortintrt IS NOT NULL AND ba.baseline_shortintrt != 0
    THEN ta.avg_shortintrt / ba.baseline_shortintrt
    ELSE NULL
  END as shortintrt_ratio
FROM transaction_averages ta
LEFT JOIN baseline_averages ba ON ta.ordertypedist = ba.ordertypedist
ORDER BY 
  shortintrt_ratio IS NULL,
  shortintrt_ratio DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: When the baseline shortintrt is zero or NULL, the ratio cannot be computed and is returned as NULL. This prevents division-by-zero errors and naturally places such rows at the end when sorting with missing ratios last.

The baseline for each ordertypedist is computed from all sentiment snapshots of that order type in the matched data, including any snapshots belonging to the transaction being compared. The phrase '(each snapshot counted once)' indicates snapshot-level granularity, not transaction-level aggregation.

alternatives.interpretation: The baseline could be computed at transaction granularity: first average shortintrt per transaction, then average those per-transaction averages within each ordertypedist. This weights each transaction equally rather than each snapshot equally, useful if transaction sample sizes differ widely.
